Dealer Sells a Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 That Really Was Driven by an Old Lady to the Grocery Store
15 photos
Photo: Justin SVT | YouTube & Apex Motors
Only driven by an old lady to the church and to the grocery store. That is one of the most common clichés when it comes to selling cars on the used car market. However, in this case, it might very well be true. This 2017 Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 hit the market after being driven around by a senior lady driver.
It may look gorgeous from ten feet away, but come closer and you'll see that it's been through thick and thin and everything in between. Justin of Justin SVT YouTube channel spotted the car in the parking lot of a dealership in Murray, Utah, and instantly realized he had seen and filmed it before, driving around in a small town in Southern Utah. At the time, it was driven around by an old lady and was in pretty rough shape. She almost never washed it, as Justin used to see it filthy and neglected.
It looked like the senior lady driver couldn't care less about the visual flaws of her 2017 Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 . She had lost the factory keyhole cover along the way, and the original black racing stripes on the aluminum hood and trunk lid were heavily sun-faded and weathered from being exposed to the brutal Utah desert sun.
Furthermore, the clear Paint Protection Film on the front end was old and had started to peel off the body panels. The GT350 looked not like an exclusive model that was worth being pampered, but like a neglected economy commuter.
Photo: Justin SVT | YouTube And the list of flaws was far from over. A scratch running down the rear driver-side quarter panel by the wheel well is still visible on the car sitting in the parking lot of Apex Motors. At one point, while the woman was driving it, the rear window on the right side was completely shattered, despite the presence of the aftermarket plastic window louvers.
The dealership tried to erase the GT350's battle scars. It removed the louvers and replaced the missing cover on the driver’s door keyhole, but a slight difference in paint tone is visible in Justin’s latest video as proof of a hard past life.
Justin recalls a mileage of roughly 42,000 miles on the blue Mustang, which now comes with a resonator delete, making the flat-plane crank V8 sound incredibly loud, but Justin points out that it is a pretty sloppy welding job. However, it definitely doesn’t sound like a car that would be driven by grandma.
First and foremost, it is what is under the hood that would scare most seniors away. The 2017 Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 is powered by the 5.2-liter flat-plane crank Voodoo V8 engine with naturally aspirated firepower.
Photo: Justin SVT | YouTube The V8 pumps out 526 horsepower (533 metric horsepower) and 429 pound-feet (582 Newton meters) of torque. That is what makes it rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.1 seconds, or just 3.9 with a one-foot rollout. It runs the quarter mile in 12.4 seconds with a trap speed of 117 mph (188 kph) and tops out at 180 mph (290 kph). A Tremec six-speed manual transmission puts the power down through the rear wheels.
The Mustang Shelby GT350 is finished in the head-turning Lightning Blue Metallic (paint code N6), introduced for the 2017 model year to replace the deeper Deep Impact Blue. However, the paint has started to lose its shine. The Mustang rides on 19-inch multi-spoke aluminum alloy wheels finished in Ebony Black.
The interior doesn't look half as bad as the exterior. The 2017 Shelby GT350 came standard with heavily bolstered Recaro sport bucket seats upholstered in a mix of Ebony cloth and Miko Alcantara inserts, while the steering wheel in leather and Alcantara sports a 12 o’clock marker and frames the speedometer scaled up to 200 mph, the tachometer with a redline starting at 8,250 rpm, along with gauges indicating oil pressure and temperature.
The nine-year-old GT350, equipped with the Track Pack, was listed for $45,995 and eventually sold, as it is no longer listed on the dealer's platform. Justin has already checked, and it comes with a clean title, but he has no idea how the dealership acquired it. Hopefully, the buyer will fix all the visual flaws that it comes with, along with mechanical issues, if any, and will treat it as it deserves.
Photo: Justin SVT | YouTube & Apex Motors Hopefully, the previous owner did maintenance work on time to keep the Voodoo V8 in a perfectly functional state. Otherwise, that poor V8 under the hood is a ticking bomb. According to Ford, it requires oil changes every 3,000 miles or less.
However, considering that Justin used to spot the car always filthy and the previous owner didn’t even bother to replace a broken window, it is very unlikely she actually followed the Ford-recommended maintenance plan.
Ford produced only 7,115 Mustang Shelby GT350s for 2017, with 6,173 standard units, like the car listed by Apex Motors, and 942 track-focused GT350Rs. Out of all 2017 models, only 1,037 cars were painted Lightning Blue, which makes the model incredibly rare.
The average price for a standard 2017 Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 sits at approximately $58,300 nowadays. However, it all comes down to condition and mileage. At over 40,000 miles, this car hasn't exactly been a garage queen.
So don't be sorry if it’s not you the one who took it home for a price under the market average. I believe you just dodged a bullet!
